# Phase 5 report (generated by `scripts/phase5_report.py`; do not edit by hand)

## Reference vocabulary and test/dev sets
- Vocabulary: 103,941 entries (94,399 from hospitals' own descriptions, 8,770 CMS HCPCS Level II, 772 CMS MS-DRG titles). Leave-one-hospital-out: a hospital's own description of its own code is never a candidate when matching that hospital's items.
- Test set: 200 items, stratified by code family (80 CPT numeric, 40 drug J-codes, 60 device/other HCPCS, 20 MS-DRG), fixed seed.
- Dev set: 3,000 items, same stratification, used only to calibrate tiering thresholds -- never used to pick the numbers reported here.

## Method comparison on the 200-item test set (top-1 accuracy)

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

| excl. 3 label-noise suspects | 197 | 0.477 | 0.574 | 0.518 | 0.122 |
| specific codes only | 132 | 0.712 | 0.742 | 0.697 | 0.152 |
| catch-all codes only (C17xx/J3490/J8499/...) | 66 | 0.0 | 0.227 | 0.152 | 0.061 |

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|

## Cost and latency per 1,000 items (measured on this test run)
| method | median latency | cost/1,000 items | notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| (a) rules+fuzzy | 189 ms | $0 | local CPU (rapidfuzz WRatio over 103,941 strings) |
| (b) embedding search | 10 ms | $0 | local, Apple MPS; encode 10ms + FAISS flat search <2ms |
| (c) LLM, candidates mode | 5902 ms | $0.175 (est., see note) | mean 309 in / 32 out tokens |
| (c) LLM, free mode | 6061 ms | $0.128 (est., see note) | no candidate list given |

**Cost note:** Azure's Retail Prices API did not return a base (non-fine-tuned) `gpt-4.1-mini` meter for this region at the time this ran (only fine-tuning meters). The $/1,000 figures use the published fine-tuned-global rate ($0.40/$1.60 per 1M in/out tokens) as a stand-in -- directionally right, not the confirmed base-model bill. Real spend is in Azure Cost Management.

## Why free mode is so much worse
LLM free mode (no candidates, model recalls a code from its own training) scored 0.12 vs 0.515 for candidates mode -- the model cannot reliably recall exact 5-digit CPT/HCPCS codes from memory; giving it a short list to choose from (built by the embedding search) is what makes it usable at all.

## Dev-hard subset: LLM on what fuzzy AND embedding both failed
Pool: 1176 dev items where fuzzy score < 0.9 AND embedding similarity < 0.9 (both non-obvious). LLM candidates-mode accuracy on a random 300-item sample of that pool: **0.23** (0.26 restricted to the model's own 'high confidence' answers, n=227).
By family: device_or_other_hcpcs: n=211 acc=0.171, drug_J: n=41 acc=0.39, cpt_numeric: n=48 acc=0.354

## Tiered strategy (calibrated on dev, applied once to test)
Target: >=95% precision per tier on dev, at >=30 supporting dev examples. Result: only the exact/fuzzy tier reached that bar on its own (threshold 0.92); the embedding tier alone never reached 95% precision on the residual pool at any threshold tested -- its real value here is as the LLM tier's candidate generator, not as a standalone confident tier. Order (exact/fuzzy first vs embedding first) made no difference on this test set, since the embedding-alone tier never activates either way.

| tier | items (of 200) | precision |
|---|---:|---:|
| exact_fuzzy | 103 | 0.903 |
| human_review | 30 | -- (sent to review) |
| llm | 67 | 0.299 |

**Overall: 170/200 items auto-resolved (85% coverage), 66.5% precision on answered items, 56.5% recall (correct / all 200).** The remaining 30 go to human review, not a silent guess.

**Honest read:** the LLM tier's own 'high confidence' label does not track actual correctness well here (29.9% precision on those 67 items) -- confidence self-report from the model is not a reliable gate on this task without a held-out check. A production version should NOT trust LLM self-reported confidence as a precision gate without validating it, exactly as shown here.

## What's NOT covered
- Test set labels were assigned as the hospital's own submitted code -- 3 were flagged during review as plausibly hospital-side coding errors (excluded in the 'excl. suspects' rows above, included in 'all 200').
- No CPT text was used anywhere (ADR-004); the vocabulary's non-CMS text is hospital-submitted, which is why coverage of CPT numeric codes depends entirely on other hospitals having described the same code, not on an official description.
